about: The evangelium of the formulary “Second Sunday after Easter” in the 1962 Roman Missal.

seg.tr: At that time, Jesus said to the Pharisees: I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd gives his life for his own sheep. But a hired worker, who is not a shepherd and to whom the sheep do not belong, sees a wolf approaching, abandons the sheep and runs away; and the wolf seizes and scatters the sheep. The hired worker, however, runs away because he is a hired worker and has no care for the sheep. I am the good shepherd; I know My sheep, and My sheep know Me, just as the Father knows Me and I know the Father; and I lay down My life for My sheep. I also have other sheep that are not from this fold; I must bring them as well, and they will hear My voice, and there will be one fold and one shepherd.

a.g: The good shepherd gives his life
who is also not a shepherd
to whom the sheep do not belong
he has no care for the sheep
just as the Father knows Me
